text:
Situation: Atropine sulfate injection has been in shortage since at least 2012-01-01. Accord Healthcare Inc. discontinued manufacture. American Regent, Inc., Amphastar Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc., Medefil, Inc., and Somerset Therapeutics, LLC all show current shortage status on FDA's list. Corvale East holds 1.8 days of 0.1 mg/mL 10 mL syringes. Corvale General holds 16.5 days and can spare 10 syringes while maintaining two weeks supply.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage database records the first posting for atropine sulfate injection on 2012-01-01, the earliest date its database holds. The database lists current shortage status for seven manufacturers as of 2026-10-21. Hospira's plant (FEI 1021343) received OAI classifications in 2010 and 2011, a Warning Letter on 2010-04-12, and its most recent inspection on 2025-02-07 was NAI.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on 0.1 mg/mL 10 mL syringes. Corvale General has sufficient stock to support a transfer without dropping below a two-week supply. Other sites have adequate inventory. Alternative suppliers are not on FDA's shortage list but their labels name no identifiable plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 10 syringes of 0.1 mg/mL 10 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director approval for transfer request.
2. Transfer 1 vial of 1 mg/mL 1 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director approval for transfer request.
3. Evaluate purchase from Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC — needs buyer approval.
4. Evaluate purchase from HF Acquisition Co LLC, DBA HealthFirst — needs buyer approval.
5. Evaluate purchase from HF Acquisition Co. LLC, DBA Health First — needs buyer approval.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or formulary substitutions; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
